notesStmt.note: This manuscript seemingly served as a portion of the copy text for the composition of November Boughs. Horace Traubel noted in With Walt Whitman in Camden that Whitman sent the copy text for the poetry section of the book to the printer on June 1, 1888, which means that the corrections on this manuscript were made sometime before then but after the poem's publication in the Herald in late February.

A newspaper clipping of Whitman's poem "Paumanok," pasted onto a larger sheet of paper, with notes and corrections in Whitman's hand. "Paumanok" was first published in the New York Herald on February 29, 1888. The poem was then published in November Boughs later that year.

lg.head: PAUMANOK.

head.del: TO THE EDITOR OF THE HERALD:

lg.l:
One side thy inland ocean laving, broad, with
copious commerce, steamers, sails,

And one the Atlantic's wind caressing, fierce or
gentle—mighty hulls dark-gliding in the
distance.

Isle of sweet brooks of drinking-water—healthy
air and soil!
Isle of the salty shore and breeze and brine!
